thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall — spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts for /v1/generate across us-west-2 since 2024-09-08T16:19:xxZ. Error rate 5xx ~6% over 5m, upstream timeout count increased. See: https://datadog.example/r/abc123

morgan: Saw the bot. I'm on it — repro-ing now. Can someone check upstream provider (edge-gateway) health?

sahil: I already queried edge metrics. Upstream provider latency to 3rd-party-llm is high; p50->p95 increased. Also a bunch of connection resets. Suspect provider flapping.

morgan: OK initiating mitigations: 1) route traffic to model-variant-v2 (lighter) 2) enable aggressive prefix KV cache for chat sessions 3) temporary autoscale bump on inference pool. Doing step 1 now.

incident-bot: morgan changed route policy for model=redwood-lg -> model-variant-v2 at 16:22:05 :white_check_mark:

liz: Heads-up — customer-visible errors reported by support team for a few customers (enterprise tier). Escalated to CS.

morgan: Noted. I'll open a customer impact note after first mitigation result.

sahil: We need to tune alerts — Datadog is firing noisy 5xx alerts for low-traffic endpoints. Proposal: only fire error-rate alert for endpoints with >=100rps or when absolute 5xx count > 50 in 5m. Also require 3m sustained window.

ana: (ana) I can take alert changes after we stabilise. Suggest we switch from percentage-only to a hybrid rule: (5xx_rate > 3% AND requests_total > 300) OR (5xx_count > 50) to prevent noisy pages.

morgan: Agree. Also add a secondary alert for upstream timeout spikes (gateway_timeouts > 30 in 5m) since those often mean provider issues.

sahil: Here's a suggested PromQL-ish query for our internal metrics (adapt when creating Datadog monitor):

```
100 * sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge-proxy",path=~"/v1/.*" ,status=~"5.."}[5m]))
/ sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge-proxy",path=~"/v1/.*"}[5m]))
```

Then alert condition: Alert when result > 3 for 5m AND sum(rate(http_requests_total[...] [5m])) > 20 OR sum(increase(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) > 50.

liz: For Datadog monitors we can add a tag filter for customer_tier:enterprise so pages go to pager only when enterprise customers see impact. Non-enterprise can be lower-severity.

danielle: I'm updating the runbook now — adding a new section "Upstream provider flapping" with checklist: 1) confirm provider status 2) shift to fallback provider / model variant 3) increase cache TTLs 4) contact provider support 5) customer comms template.

morgan: Update: after routing to model-variant-v2, 5xx rate dropped from 6% -> 1.8% within 3m. Timeouts also dropped. Autoscale kept latency stable.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert auto-resolved at 16:28:12 — condition no longer met.

morgan: Handing off to sahil for post-incident follow-up and alert tuning. @sahil you're oncall for next 1h?

sahil: Yep, I'm taking it. Will do the Datadog monitor changes and spin up a dashboard.

ana: I'll own the dashboard creation (5xx rate, upstream latency, timeout counts, requests by model variant). Plan: create a heatmap + per-endpoint table and an alert rule stub. ETA 2 hours.

morgan: I'll draft the customer impact note for CS with affected windows and mitigation steps. Rough numbers: ~12 customers saw errors, median error duration ~6m.

liz: Thanks. I'll prepare the CS message and flag customers who need follow-up.

sahil: Quick note on tuning: let's implement a two-tier alerting approach — page SREs for sustained (>5m) high-severity incidents (enterprise impact OR absolute 5xx count >100). For transient spikes, send an Ops digest channel message only. That reduces pager fatigue.

danielle: Agreed. Also add an automated suppression for known scheduled jobs that generate 5xx during deploy windows.

morgan: Action items recap: 1) sahil -> update Datadog monitors (hybrid rule + enterprise tagging + paging thresholds) 2) ana -> create dashboard panels and save as "SRE / 5xx ops" 3) danielle -> edit runbook (Upstream provider flapping) 4) morgan -> customer impact note for CS 5) liz -> CS comms and triage list.

sahil: I'll put a PR with monitor JSON and screenshot of alert conditions. Also will add a muted-window rule while we tune.

ana: Dashboard will include a query for upstream provider latency broken down by provider_id so we can attribute upstream failures quickly.

morgan: Thanks all. Reopen thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Reminder: oncall-rotations will be notified to update schedule if needed.

oncall-rotations: Morgan marked incident handled and shifted follow-up to sahil for 1h.

sahil: Follow-up: created monitor draft, uploading PR at https://git.example/r/monitors/987. Will iterate with ana on exact query thresholds.

ana: Dashboard PR: https://dashboards.example/p/123 - includes the new 5xx heatmap and an allowed-threshold overlay.

morgan: Closing loop: runbook PR merged, monitor PR pending review. Will review once sahil pushes final thresholds. Good job team.
